name: Propofol
executiveSummary: IV hypnotic. Adult induction **1–2.5 mg/kg**; ped **2–2.5 mg/kg**. ICU sedation: **25–75 mcg/kg/min** or **0.25–4 mg/kg/h**. NICU: highly restricted — if used, low bolus **1–2 mg/kg** / minimal titrated infusion.
indications:
## Indications

- Anesthetic induction/maintenance; sedation in ventilated patients.
- Not analgesic — combine opioid if pain.

## Precautions

- Hypotension, apnea, injection-site pain. Propofol infusion syndrome (rare) at high/prolonged doses.
- Caution in lipid disorders / pancreatitis.
- Emulsion: aseptic technique; discard **6–12 h** after opening.

> May be used undiluted (10 mg/mL) or diluted in D5W (= **2 mg/mL**).

adulto.dose: Induction **1–2.5 mg/kg IV**. Sedation **25–75 mcg/kg/min** (equiv. orient. **1.5–4.5 mg/kg/h**) titrated.
adulto.administration: Slow IV bolus or infusion; dedicated line preferred.
adulto.notes: Monitor BP, triglycerides, and lactate if infusion >48 h.

pediatrico.dose: Bolus **2–2.5 mg/kg**. Continuous infusion **0.25–4 mg/kg/h** (common max peri-extubation sedation ~48 h).
pediatrico.notes: Opened line stability ~6 h. Store per package insert.

neonatal.dose: Highly restricted. If anesthesia/procedure: bolus **1–2 mg/kg IV** slow; infusion specialist only at minimal titrated doses (e.g. **0.5–2 mg/kg/h**).
neonatal.administration: IV with secured airway / full monitoring.
neonatal.notes: Prefer validated NICU alternatives when available.

stability:
## Stability

- Aseptic chain. Discard remainder 6–12 h after opening. Dilution in D5W: ~12 h room temperature (local guide).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Apnea, hypotension, bradycardia, local pain, hypertriglyceridemia, infusion syndrome (rare).
